sources.title: LoRA (machine learning) - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models and other deep neural networks. Introduced in 2021 by researchers at Microsoft, LoRA enables adaptation of pre-trained models to specific tasks while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and trainable parameters than traditional full model fine-tuning. [1]

sources.title: LoRA Explained: Enhancing AI Models with Low-Rank Adaptation
sources.snippet: Photo by Adi Goldstein on Unsplash LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a technique used to fine-tune large language models, particularly those based on transformers, to reduce the computational and memory overhead. PAPER LoRA is typically applied to models already pre-trained on a large corpus of data. Pre-training is the initial stage where the model is trained with a massive corpus of text data ...
